title: Product PRD: Unified Inference — Q4 Product Overview, Roadmap & Pricing
author: Aisha Patel
content:
H1. Product PRD: Unified Inference — Q4 Product Overview, Roadmap & Pricing

Short summary:
This document consolidates the product overview, PRD-level requirements, high-level design considerations, roadmap themes, pricing/packaging options, and release notes for the Unified Inference product direction for Q4 2026. It is intended for cross-functional stakeholders (product, engineering, sales, marketing, and support) and serves as the single-source reference for upcoming releases and commercial positioning.

H2. Background and problem statement
- As customers mature from prototypes to production, they require a single inference platform that provides predictable latency, cost controls, and consistent operational tooling across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Current fragmentation across model variants, deployment modes, and cost controls increases integration overhead for engineering teams and creates unpredictable unit economics.

H2. Goals and success metrics (OKRs)
- Goal: Deliver a Unified Inference experience that reduces time-to-production for model-powered features and improves cost predictability.
- Success metrics (measurable):
  - Reduce average 95th percentile latency for small-generation workloads by 20% (baseline: 240ms).
  - Reduce per-token cost for typical single-session LLM workloads by 15% via batching and prefix caching improvements.
  - Achieve 90% adoption of the new model-routing policy for qualifying customers within 3 months of release.
  - NPS (product) > 60 for teams using Dedicated and Private tiers.

H2. Key features in scope
- Unified API surface: single generation/chat/embedding endpoint with explicit deployment_targets (hosted, dedicated, private).
- Cost-aware model routing: dynamic routing policies that balance latency and price with customer-configurable SLAs.
- Smart batching & KV-prefix caching improvements with per-tenant tuning profiles.
- Packaging & pricing tiers aligned to usage patterns: Developer (self-serve), Team (reserved bursts), Enterprise (dedicated + private).
- Console updates: per-route cost breakdowns, rollout control plane (canary, A/B), and drift detection for model outputs.

H2. Requirements (high level)
- Functional requirements:
  1. API: Single endpoint supporting generation, chat, embeddings, and structured outputs. Must include parameters: model, deployment_target, routing_policy, max_tokens, stream.
  2. Routing: Support declarative routing policies with rules for latency_target_ms, cost_weight, fallback_models.
  3. Batching/cache: Per-tenant config for batch_size_target (default 16), prefix_cache_ttl (default 1h), and KV eviction policies.
  4. Observability: Per-request token-level cost, 50ms sampling for tail-latency tracing, and per-model quality alerts tied to eval prompt-sets.
  5. Security: Support KMS for private deployments, RBAC for rollout controls, and audit logs retained for 90 days (configurable for Enterprise).

- Non-functional requirements:
  - Availability: 99.95% for Hosted API across primary regions (SLA target for Enterprise Dedicated is 99.9%).
  - Latency: p95 generation latency target under 300ms for small (<=256 tokens) workloads on hosted and dedicated SKUs.
  - Scalability: Support scale-to-zero for low-traffic tenants and burst-to-dedicated pools within 60s.
  - Backwards compatibility: Existing client libraries must continue to function; migration hooks provided for opt-in routing policies.

H2. Acceptance criteria
- End-to-end test-suite passes with performance gates: p50/p95/p99 under target for representative workloads.
- Customer beta (10 customers across SMB and Enterprise) complete 30-day evaluation with documented feedback.
- Pricing & packaging validated with sales (commission/discount impact analyzed).

H2. Design & architecture notes
- Overview: Unified Control Plane (UCP) manages routing policies, rollout state, and tenancy configs; Serving Runtime remains optimized for kernels and quantization variants.
- Components:
  - API Gateway: validates requests, enriches with tenant config, and proxies to UCP.
  - UCP Policy Engine: evaluates declarative routing rules and issues route decisions.
  - Runtime Router: performs real-time selection of model variant and queue placement (hot path within 2ms).
  - Observability pipeline: emits traces, token costs, and quality signals to Console and internal data platform.
- Data model: routing_policy is a JSON blob (stored as opaque config) with required keys: name, rules[], default_fallback.
- Security boundaries: tenant keys and private deployment credentials separated from control plane; secrets flow uses KMS-wrapped credentials.

H2. Design trade-offs considered
- Centralized policy evaluation vs. edge decisions: we choose centralized UCP for easier rollback and auditability, accepting slightly higher control-plane latency (mitigated by caching decisions at the API gateway for 30s).
- Aggressive batching to save cost vs. latency SLOs: implement adaptive batching with SLO-aware timeouts.

H2. Roadmap & themes (quarterly view)
- Q1 2026 (complete): Foundational runtime improvements, prefix caching v1, initial routing prototypes.
- Q2 2026 (complete): API consolidation, Dedicated SKU launch, console cost breakdowns.
- Q3 2026 (complete): Smart batching v2, model-routing policy MVP, pricing experiments with Team tier.
- Q4 2026 (current):
  - Launch: Cost-aware routing GA and per-tenant batching profiles.
  - Deliverables: Console rollout controls (canary/A-B), private deployment KMS integration, and quality alert pipelines.
  - Commercial: Finalize Team & Enterprise pricing tiers and partner enablement materials.
- Q1 2027 (planned): Autoscaling policy marketplace, policy templates for regulated workloads, expanded region coverage (APAC).

H2. Pricing & packaging notes
- Guiding principles:
  - Align pricing to customer value (latency & predictability) rather than raw GPU hours.
  - Provide clear upgrade paths from Developer -> Team -> Enterprise.
  - Ensure pricing supports channel discounts and committed-use economics for Dedicated.

- Proposed SKUs (examples):
  1. Developer (self-serve): pay-as-you-go, hosted API credits, suitable for prototyping.
     - Billing: per-token generation + per-embedding unit. Free tier: 100k tokens / month trial.
  2. Team (committed bursts): monthly commit (e.g., $5k/mo) with burst capacity & reduced token rate. Includes per-route cost dashboards and 30-day data retention.
  3. Enterprise: Dedicated GPU pools + Private deployment option. Pricing: baseline platform fee + committed capacity (GPU-months) + overage token rate. Includes 99.9% SLA, audit logs, and extended retention.

- Discounts & add-ons:
  - Committed discounts: 15-40% depending on term and size.
  - Add-ons: Extended observability retention, compliance evidence package, premium support (SLA 1h).

H2. Release notes — v3.4.0 (2026-12-01)
- GA: Cost-aware model routing (policy engine) — supports latency_target_ms and cost_weight.
- GA: Per-tenant batching profiles and prefix_cache_ttl controls.
- Console: Rollout controls (canary and A/B) exposed in UI and API.
- Private: KMS integration for customer-managed keys in Private deployments.
- Observability: Token-level cost breakdown and quality alerting linked to eval prompt-sets.
- Fixed: Several p95 regression issues on long-context workloads; improved kernel selection heuristics.

H2. Rollout plan (high level)
1. Internal dogfooding (2 weeks): product, eng, and solutions teams validate core workflows and migration paths.
2. Beta customers (4-6 customers, 30 days): collect performance and UX feedback; iterate on routing policy defaults.
3. Gradual GA (region-by-region, 2 weeks each): enable cost-aware routing by default for new Tenant signups; provide opt-in for existing tenants for 60 days.
4. Full GA: flip default routing to cost-aware for qualifying workloads; update pricing pages and partner materials.

H2. Rollback & mitigation steps
- If routing policy causes customer regressions, switch tenant to legacy routing via UCP -> immediate effect.
- Hotfix: revert policy engine version in UCP and re-run canary.
- Communication: incident template to notify affected customers with remediation ETA and mitigation steps.

H2. Open risks & mitigations
- Risk: Customers may experience quality regressions when switching models for cost reasons.
  - Mitigation: Require per-tenant quality guardrail (eval prompt-set) before enabling cost-weight > 0.
- Risk: Complexity of pricing leading to objections in sales cycles.
  - Mitigation: Publish clear example invoices and TCO calculator embedded in Sales enablement pack.

H2. Appendix: representative config examples
- Example routing policy (declarative):
  {
    "name": "latency-prefer",
    "rules": [
      { "match": "request.load < 0.5", "action": "prefer-low-cost", "cost_weight": 0.6 },
      { "match": "request.latency_target_ms <= 200", "action": "prefer-low-latency", "cost_weight": 0.1 }
    ],
    "default_fallback": "redwood-gpt-4-quant"
  }

- Sample SLO table:
  | Metric | Target | Measurement |
  |---|---:|---:|
  | p95 generation latency (<=256 tokens) | 300ms | synthetic workload + production sampling |
  | Hosted API availability | 99.95% | region health metrics |
  | Time-to-burst (dedicated) | <=60s | deployment traces |

H2. Next steps
- Finalize pricing examples and publish Sales enablement by 2026-12-10.
- Complete region-by-region GA plan and customer comms templates by 2026-12-15.
- Schedule post-GA retrospective and collect adoption metrics 30 days after GA.
